1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant is the complainant in Case Crime No.141/2015 and FIR No.0113/2015, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 418 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at Police Station Surajpur, District Gautam Budha Nagar.
The said FIR culminated into Case No.1642/2016 in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Gautam Budh Nagar.

entities.text: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Gautam Budh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The facts which led to initiation of the above- mentioned proceedings may be briefly noticed.

Respondent nos.2 and 3 (the accused) launched a project known as Mist Avenue Pvt. Ltd. in Sector 143, NOIDA, allegedly with misleading advertisements offering to the public at large for booking commercial flats/offices/space/villas etc., which was launched in the year 2012.
The appellant also booked a commercial unit and in due course, deposited a sum of Rs.32,43,840/-.
It is not necessary to delve into the minute details of the contractual obligations between the parties.
Suffice it to say that, according to the appellant, the respondents, in collusion with the developing authority NOIDA, abruptly changed the original lay out plan to obtain wrongful gains.

Despite the payment of preferential location charges, the proposed revised plan did not provide such a space to the appellant and thus, diminished the commercial utility of the unit which was to be allotted to him.
He further alleged that no allotment letter was issued and no construction was commenced at the site despite tall promises made by the developer.

sentences.text:
With these allegations, the appellant filed an application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and pursuant to the directions issued by the learned Judicial Magistrate,
the subject FIR was registered.

After the chargesheet was filed, respondent nos.2 and 3 were summoned vide an order dated 07.05.2016.
5.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. The High Court, while accepting the claim of respondent nos.2 and 3 that there was an arbitral agreement between the parties, took the view that the appellant ought not to have lodged the FIR straightaway without first resorting to the remedies as agreed to between the parties.

Consequently,
the FIR, chargesheet and the summoning order have been quashed vide the impugned judgment dated 13.12.2017.
7.
The aggrieved appellant is before us.

When the matter came up for hearing on 29.09.2022,
respondent nos.2 and 3 offered to deposit a sum of Rs.32,43,840/-, i.e., the principal amount invested by the appellant in the project in question.
They also agreed to deposit a reasonable rate of interest with the Registry.
Subsequently, a demand draft in the sum of Rs.40 lakhs, which includes the principal amount of Rs.32,43,840/-, has been deposited with the Registry.
8. It was in light of these subsequent events that the parties were suggested to explore the possibility of an amicable settlement.

9. Learned senior counsel/counsel for the parties jointly state that the appellant has no objection to the quashing of the proceedings, provided that respondents pay a lump sum amount of Rs.52 lakhs to him, which shall include the amount of Rs.40 lakhs, which is already lying deposited with the Registry of this Court.

10. This offer is acceptable to learned counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3.
11.

In this view of the matter and in the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, with a further clarification that this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the other criminal proceedings pending against respondent nos.2 and 3 before any Forum, we deem it appropriate to dispose of this appeal in the following terms:
(i) The Registry is directed to release the amount of Rs.40 lakhs along with interest accrued thereupon in favour of the appellant forthwith.
(ii) The exact amount to be received by the appellant from the Registry shall be informed by his counsel to the counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3.

On receipt of such information, respondent nos.2 and 3 will pay the balance amount (to make the total Ashish Gupta vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141540291/
2 Rs.52 lakhs) within four weeks from the date of information.

sentences.text: 12. On receipt of that amount, the present appeal will be deemed to have been dismissed as withdrawn.

13. However, if respondent nos.2 and 3 fail to pay the balance amount within four weeks, as directed above, the instant appeal shall be deemed to have been allowed and, in that case, the criminal prosecution launched by the appellant against respondent nos.2 and 3 shall stand revived.
14.
The appeal is disposed of in the above terms.
